## Sources
- **Clone.** Metrolist was shallow-cloned from https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist (the official repo, GPL-3.0) into `C:\Users\droid\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\--psf-Home-Desktop-Multiplatform-Music-player\04bbb583-faaf-4a88-9a62-5827ef684e67\scratchpad\Metrolist`. HEAD is `28fa8f0`, dated 2026-09-23. Paths below are relative to that folder.
- **InnerTubeX.** Networking and auth headers moved out of Metrolist into InnerTubeX, a separate library: https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/InnerTubeX (also GPL-3.0). Metrolist pins `v0.7.0` (`gradle/libs.versions.toml:34`; changelog line 6 "Migrated networking to InnerTubeX").
  - I read InnerTubeX HEAD through WebFetch, which summarises pages with a small model. Line numbers marked "~" are approximate, and v0.7.0 may differ slightly from HEAD.
- Nothing in Monolist was touched. No cookie or token values appear anywhere below, only names.

---
## 1. Login screen and WebView setup
File: `app/src/main/kotlin/com/metrolist/music/ui/screens/LoginScreen.kt`

- **Routes.** `composable("login")` shows `LoginScreen(navController)`. `composable("switch_channel")` shows `LoginScreen(isSwitchingChannel = true)` (`ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt:411-420`). The entry points are in `ui/screens/settings/AccountSettings.kt:296-313`.
- **WebView.** It is a plain `android.webkit.WebView` inside Compose `AndroidView` (LoginScreen.kt:305-362).
- **Settings** (L341-347):
  - `javaScriptEnabled = true` and `domStorageEnabled = true`.
  - Zoom settings, and nothing else.
  - **No custom user agent is set on the login WebView.** It sends the stock Android WebView UA.
  - No `setAcceptThirdPartyCookies` and no `WebChromeClient`.
  - The only `userAgentString` in the whole app is on the separate BotGuard/PoToken WebView (`utils/potoken/PoTokenWebView.kt:76`), which never loads Google sign-in.
- **JS bridge.** `addJavascriptInterface(jsInterface, "Android")` (L348). The interface class `LoginJsInterface` exposes `onRetrieveVisitorData`, `onRetrieveDataSyncId` and `onRetrieveAuthUser` (L560-579).
- **URL loaded** (L353-359):
  - Fresh login: `https://accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin?continue=https%3A%2F%2Fmusic.youtube.com`. There are no other query parameters: no `service=youtube`, no `passive`, no `hl`.
  - Channel switch: `https://music.youtube.com`, after re-injecting the saved cookies (see §6).
- **"Settings that make Google accept it".** There are none beyond JS and DOM storage.
  - Google's 2021 embedded-webview block applies to the **OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint**, not to `ServiceLogin` (https://developers.googleblog.com/upcoming-security-changes-to-googles-oauth-20-authorization-endpoint-in-embedded-webviews/).
  - Metrolist's current code implies Android WebView + `ServiceLogin` still works in Sept 2026. That is inferred from shipping code; I found no statement of it.
  - The separate Jan-2021 block on "embedded frameworks" names CEF (https://developers.googleblog.com/guidance-to-developers-affected-by-our-effort-to-block-less-secure-browsers-and-applications/). That is the one that bites desktop embeds (§9).
- **URL handling** (`shouldOverrideUrlLoading`, L311-329):
  - http/https stay in the WebView.
  - `intent:` URIs are parsed and started as an external BROWSABLE activity, with component and selector nulled.
  - Every other scheme is swallowed.
  - This is the fix for issue #3183 (`net::ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME` when Google redirected to a Play Store / YT Music intent URL): https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist/issues/3183.
- **Other UI.**
  - Back navigates the WebView history while authenticating (L477-481).
  - The error dialog's Retry button calls `webView.reload()` (L459-475).

## 2. How success is detected
- **Trigger.** `onPageFinished` fires `handleAuthenticatedPage()` whenever the finished URL has scheme `https` and host exactly `music.youtube.com` (L331-339). That is the landing page of the `continue=` redirect.
- **Polling.** `extractAuthData()` (L119-179) retries up to 20 times, each with a 1 s JS timeout and a 500 ms delay, so roughly 10-30 s in total. Each round it:
  - reads cookies: `CookieManager.getInstance().getCookie("https://music.youtube.com")` (L124);
  - reads page config by injecting `javascript:` URLs that call the bridge with `window.yt.config_.VISITOR_DATA`, `window.yt.config_.DATASYNC_ID` and `String(window.yt.config_.SESSION_INDEX||0)` (L139-150).
- **Success condition** (L160-169):
  - The cookie map contains `SAPISID`, **and**
  - `VISITOR_DATA` is non-blank.
- **Stored values.**
  - `dataSyncId` is stored as `DATASYNC_ID.substringBefore("||")` (L167).
  - `authUser` is `SESSION_INDEX` digits only, defaulting to "0" (L168).
- **On timeout.** It logs `authCookie=…, visitorData=…` as booleans only, and shows `authentication_data_extraction_failed`.
- **Server check.** `finalizeLogin()` (L181-231) pushes the four values into the `YouTube` singleton and calls `YouTube.accountInfo()`. If that fails, it shows `login_failed_with_error`.

## 3. Which cookies, for which domain
- **Domain and format.** Cookies are read **only for `https://music.youtube.com`** (L124).
  - Android's `CookieManager.getCookie` returns every cookie that would be sent to that URL: host-only `music.youtube.com` cookies plus all `Domain=.youtube.com` cookies.
  - It returns them as one `name=value; name=value` string with no attributes.
  - It includes HttpOnly cookies. That is platform behaviour, not shown in Metrolist code.
  - `.google.com` cookies are **not** captured.
- **Stored as-is.** The whole string is kept unfiltered (L193). It is parsed by `parseCookieString`, which splits on `"; "` (`innertube/src/main/kotlin/com/metrolist/innertube/utils/Utils.kt:58-66`).
- **Metrolist's only explicit check is `SAPISID`.** It appears in:
  - `LoginScreen.kt:160`;
  - `isLoggedIn` in `AccountSettings.kt:93-95` and `utils/SyncUtils.kt:271-281`;
  - the token editor validation (`AccountSettings.kt:238-247`).
- **InnerTubeX hash source.** It resolves the value to hash from `SAPISID`, falling back to `__Secure-3PAPISID` and then `__Secure-1PAPISID` (InnerTubeX `InnerTube.kt` `resolveSapisidValue`, ~L265).
- **www.youtube.com vs music.youtube.com.**
  - Metrolist keeps **one cookie string and sends it to both hosts**. InnerTubeX's `ytClient()` picks the API base and Origin per client:
    - `WEB_REMIX` goes to `music.youtube.com/youtubei/v1`;
    - `MWEB` goes to `m.youtube.com`;
    - `WEB_CREATOR` goes to `studio.youtube.com`;
    - everything else, including `WEB`, goes to `www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1`.
  - It then attaches the same `Cookie` header, with `PREF=hl=..&gl=..` merged in by `injectPrefCookie`.
  - It computes `Authorization: SAPISIDHASH <ts>_<sha1("<ts> <sapisid> <origin>")>` using **the origin of the host being called**.
  - It also sends `X-Goog-AuthUser`, `X-Goog-Visitor-Id`, `X-Origin` and `Referer`.
  - Result: a login landing on music.youtube.com yields `.youtube.com` session cookies that also authenticate www.youtube.com calls.
  - Sources: InnerTubeX `src/commonMain/kotlin/com/metrolist/innertubex/InnerTube.kt` (companion constants and the `ytClient` function, ~L326-364 / ~L453-475; the fetch tool gave inconsistent line numbers).
  - `sw.js_data` (the visitor-data endpoint) is fetched from www.youtube.com, falling back to the music.youtube.com homepage (InnerTubeX `fetchFreshVisitorData`, ~L1396-1447).
  - InnerTubeX sends only a single-scheme `SAPISIDHASH`. There is no 1P/3P variant.

## 4. visitorData / dataSyncId / authUser / account info
- **At login.**
  - `VISITOR_DATA`, `DATASYNC_ID` and `SESSION_INDEX` come from `window.yt.config_` via the JS bridge (§2).
  - Account info comes from `YouTube.accountInfo()`. That POSTs `account/account_menu` with `WEB_REMIX` (music.youtube.com) and parses `actions[0].openPopupAction.popup.multiPageMenuRenderer.header.activeAccountHeaderRenderer`, giving name, email, channelHandle and last thumbnail. Code: `innertube/.../YouTube.kt:3167-3177` and `models/response/AccountMenuResponse.kt:34-46`.
- **At startup** (`App.kt:196-251`):
  - DataStore flows feed the `YouTube` singleton.
  - If visitorData is missing, `YouTube.visitorData()` fetches a fresh value and persists it (L199-213).
  - dataSyncId is normalised on load (L220-227): kept if it has no `||`; the part before `||` if it ends with `||`; otherwise the part after `||`.
  - `authUser` defaults to "0" (L232).
- **How they are sent** (InnerTubeX):
  - `dataSyncId` becomes `context.user.onBehalfOfUser` (`models/Context.kt`). On browse it is sent when login is used; on player it is sent when `client.loginSupported`.
  - `authUser` becomes the `X-Goog-AuthUser` header.
  - `visitorData` becomes `X-Goog-Visitor-Id`.
- **Account name refresh.** `HomeViewModel.kt:656-663` and `757-773` reload the account name and avatar via `accountInfo()` whenever the stored cookie changes.

## 5. Storage
- **Plain Jetpack DataStore.** The file is `preferencesDataStore(name = "settings")` (`utils/DataStore.kt:45`), i.e. `filesDir/datastore/settings.preferences_pb`.
- **Keys** (`constants/PreferenceKeys.kt:516-527`): `innerTubeCookie`, `visitorData`, `dataSyncId`, `innerTubeAuthUser`, `accountName`, `accountEmail`, `accountChannelHandle`, plus the toggle `useLoginForBrowse`.
- **Not encrypted.** By contrast, the Discord token *is* Android-Keystore/AES encrypted (`discord/DiscordTokenStore.kt:38-61`).
- **Backups.**
  - `android:allowBackup="true"` (`AndroidManifest.xml:32-37`), and `res/xml/backup_rules.xml` does not exclude the datastore. So the cookie can travel in Android cloud backup and device transfer.
  - Metrolist's own backup/restore carries the settings file. On restore it can:
    - strip the four auth keys (`viewmodels/BackupRestoreViewModel.kt:272-295`);
    - preview the account by hand-building a SAPISIDHASH `account_menu` call to music.youtube.com (L433-460).
- **Write then restart.** After a successful write, `finalizeLogin` clears the WebView history, cache and form data, then calls `CookieManager.flush()`. **The WebView cookie jar is kept.** It then restarts the whole process (`Runtime.getRuntime().exit(0)`, L204-218) so every component picks up the new session.
- **"Log in with token"** (`AccountSettings.kt:188-253`, `viewmodels/AccountSettingsViewModel.kt:81-112`) is a manual paste of the same fields in a `***INNERTUBE COOKIE*** =…` template. It is only accepted if the cookie contains `SAPISID`. This is Metrolist's cookie-import path, equivalent to our `cookieimport`.

## 6. Account switching / brand accounts
- **Listing channels.**
  - `YouTube.accountsList()` POSTs `account/accounts_list` with the **`WEB` client**, i.e. `https://www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/account/accounts_list` (`innertube/.../InnerTube.kt:257`, `YouTube.kt:3179-3184`).
  - The response is parsed generically for every `accountItem` / `accountItemRenderer` (`innertube/.../models/YouTubeAccount.kt:21-66`). Fields read:
    - `accountName`, `accountByline`, `channelHandle`, `accountPhoto`, `isSelected`;
    - from `selectActiveIdentityEndpoint.supportedTokens[]`: `accountSigninToken.signinUrl`, `pageIdToken.pageId`, `datasyncIdToken.datasyncIdToken`.
- **Picker flow** (`LoginScreen.kt:233-266`, `390-457`):
  - After the first login, if more than one channel exists, a picker appears. The current channel is matched by `pageId` or datasyncId against the page's `DATASYNC_ID`.
  - Choosing a non-selected channel loads its `signinUrl` in the same WebView. A relative URL is prefixed with `https://music.youtube.com`.
  - Stage `SwitchingAccount` then waits for the next music.youtube.com page finish. It re-extracts cookies and ytcfg and **overrides `dataSyncId` with the chosen account's `datasyncIdToken` before `||`** (L282-288).
  - Changelog v13.4.2: "Added back support for choosing an account upon login" (`changelog.md:166`). Related: https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist/issues/3194.
- **"Switch YouTube channel" from settings.**
  - Runs the same screen with `isSwitchingChannel=true`.
  - `restoreYouTubeCookies()` writes each saved `name=value` back into `CookieManager` for `https://music.youtube.com` as `Domain=.youtube.com; Path=/; Secure` (L587-600), then loads music.youtube.com. The user does not type a password again.
  - If the channel list is empty or fails, it shows `youtube_channels_failed` (L243-253).

## 7. Sign-out
`App.forgetAccount()` (`App.kt:331-370`), called from `AccountSettingsViewModel.logoutKeepData` / `logoutAndClearLibraryData` (L49-73):
- removes the seven DataStore keys;
- nulls the in-memory cookie, visitorData and dataSyncId, and sets authUser to "0";
- calls `CookieManager.removeAllCookies()` + `flush()` "to prevent auto-relogin";
- optionally wipes the library.

**No server-side sign-out or revocation.** Nothing calls accounts.google.com Logout. The Google session stays valid until it expires or the user removes the device in their Google account.

## 8. Refresh / expiry detection
**Metrolist has none.**
- "Logged in" means only that `SAPISID` is present in the stored string (`SyncUtils.kt:271-281`, `AccountSettings.kt:93-95`).
- The Ktor client that Metrolist builds (`innertube/.../InnerTube.kt:138-190`) installs no cookie plugin. InnerTubeX reads no `Set-Cookie`, does no `__Secure-*PSIDTS` rotation, makes no `RotateCookies` or `accounts.google.com` calls, and does not check `responseContext` `logged_in`. (WebFetch summary of InnerTubeX `InnerTube.kt`.)
- InnerTubeX only offers `clearSessionIfMatches` / `replaceSession` for callers, with generation-based cancellation of in-flight requests.
- Failures surface only indirectly:
  - `accountInfo()` failure is just reported (`HomeViewModel.kt:660-662`).
  - Playback errors containing `LOGIN_REQUIRED` / `403` / "confirm your age" show "Explicit playback works better with a logged-in account" (`ui/player/PlaybackError.kt:64-80`).
  - A cookie that fails to parse triggers `forgetAccount` (`App.kt:243-249`).
- **Why a static snapshot survives (my inference).** The login WebView is torn down and the process restarted right after capture, so no live browser tab keeps rotating that session. This matches yt-dlp's advice: YouTube "rotates account cookies frequently on open YouTube browser tabs"; export from a private window, then close it (https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors). The channel-switch flow does reopen music.youtube.com with the saved cookies, and could rotate them. Unverified.

## 9. Blocking, issues, changelog (2026)
- **No Metrolist issue about "This browser or app may not be secure".** Related ones:
  - #4406 (open, 2026-09-23): asks to replace the in-WebView email/password entry with official Google OAuth. No maintainer reply visible. https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist/issues/4406
  - #3183: intent-scheme error (§1).
  - #3578: logged out after the v13.4.1 update (closed, cause not visible). https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist/issues/3578
  - #4216: crash at login in v13.6.1. https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist/issues/4216
  - #4192 / #4242: "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" even while logged in (closed; WebFetch showed no maintainer replies). https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist/issues/4192, https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist/issues/4242
- **Changelog.** Only generic lines: "Improved login, account loading…" (v13.7.0, `changelog.md:9`) and "Fixed login, logout…" (v13.6.1, L83). There is no UA-spoof workaround anywhere in the code.
- **Desktop embeds are the real risk.**
  - Google has blocked sign-in from embedded frameworks (CEF etc.) since 2021-01-04 (Google Developers Blog, above).
  - WebView2 users hit "This browser or app may not be secure" (https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/1584, 2021).
  - Metrolist's KMP desktop version is alpha and closed (Discord/donor only), and I found no public description of its desktop login (https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist/issues/3853).

## 10. Relevance to "stream via www.youtube.com with the login" (brief; another topic may cover it)
- **Player requests carry the login.** InnerTubeX calls `ytClient(..., setLogin = true)` for player, so cookie + SAPISIDHASH + `onBehalfOfUser` go out, but only for clients with `loginSupported = true`.
- **Which clients support login** (per the InnerTubeX `models/YouTubeClient.kt` summary; please verify):
  - Login-capable: WEB, WEB_SAFARI, MWEB, WEB_REMIX, WEB_EMBEDDED_PLAYER, TVHTML5, WEB_CREATOR.
  - Not login-capable: ANDROID*, IOS*, ANDROID_VR*, VISIONOS*.
  - So **Monolist's current anonymous VISIONOS tier cannot carry the login.** A signed-in www.youtube.com stream needs the WEB/WEB_SAFARI/MWEB/TV family.
- **Those clients need a PO token and the player-JS cipher.** Metrolist gets its PO token from a BotGuard WebView, keyed by videoId + visitorData. It ignores the `cookie` argument (`utils/InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:181-205`).
- **yt-dlp warnings** (wiki above):
  - "By using your account with yt-dlp, you run the risk of it being banned".
  - Rough limits: about 300 videos/h as a guest vs about 2000/h with an account.
research.recommendation:
Build the Metrolist login shape ourselves (MIT, no copying): one sign-in window, one cookie jar used against both hosts, feed on music.youtube.com and streaming on www.youtube.com.

1. **Sign-in window.**
   - Load `https://accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin?continue=https%3A%2F%2Fmusic.youtube.com`.
   - Treat the first finished navigation whose host is music.youtube.com as the success trigger.
   - Poll for up to about 30 s until the cookie jar has SAPISID (or __Secure-3PAPISID) and `ytcfg` VISITOR_DATA is non-empty.
   - Read VISITOR_DATA, DATASYNC_ID (store the part before `||`) and SESSION_INDEX (use it as X-Goog-AuthUser) by running script in the page.
   - Read cookies through the native cookie API for `https://music.youtube.com`, never `document.cookie`, which misses the HttpOnly SID family.
2. **Engine choice on Windows/MinGW.**
   - Qt WebEngine is out (no MinGW build).
   - Qt WebView cannot return cookie values, and its WebView2 backend needs MSVC.
   - So the only route is a hand-hosted WebView2, e.g. webview/webview (MIT, MinGW), with `ICoreWebView2CookieManager::GetCookies` and `ExecuteScript`. That is the half-day spike already in CONNECTIONS_DESIGN.md.
   - The spike's first question is whether Google shows "This browser or app may not be secure" for WebView2 without a UA change. Metrolist needs no spoof on Android, but desktop embedded frameworks have been blocked since 2021.
   - If it is blocked, a UA spoof circumvents Google's policy, so that is the owner's call. Keep cookie import (Metrolist's own "Log in with token" does the same thing) as the always-available fallback.
   - macOS: a WKWebView sheet can reuse the same state machine.
3. **After capture.**
   - Validate with `account/account_menu` on WEB_REMIX.
   - Keep the WebView2 profile folder only if you need channel switching. Otherwise delete it, so no live tab rotates the snapshot.
   - Store the cookie string, visitorData, dataSyncId, authUser and account name/email/handle in our existing secretstore. Metrolist keeps them in a plaintext DataStore that Android backups include; do not repeat that.
4. **Feed (YTM).** Send the cookie, SAPISIDHASH with origin `https://music.youtube.com`, X-Goog-AuthUser and `context.user.onBehalfOfUser = dataSyncId` on WEB_REMIX browse. Home becomes personalised when "use login for browse" is on, which is Metrolist's default.
5. **Streaming (www).** Reuse the same cookie on a login-capable www client (WEB / WEB_SAFARI / MWEB / TV) with SAPISIDHASH computed for origin `https://www.youtube.com`.
   - This needs a PO token and n/sig handling. Our anonymous VISIONOS tier cannot use the login.
   - Warn the owner about the account-ban and rate-limit risk yt-dlp documents.
6. **Brand accounts.**
   - Call `www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/account/accounts_list` with the WEB client and walk every accountItem for `selectActiveIdentityEndpoint.supportedTokens` (signinUrl, pageId, datasyncIdToken).
   - Switching means loading the signinUrl in the sign-in window, then re-capturing cookies and using the chosen datasyncId.
   - Without a window, just swapping `onBehalfOfUser` may be enough for reads. That is untested.
7. **Sign-out and expiry.**
   - Sign-out: clear secretstore and the WebView2 profile, and tell the user the Google session is not revoked server-side (Metrolist does not revoke it either).
   - Expiry: add what Metrolist lacks. Check `account_menu` at startup and read responseContext `logged_in` / 401 / LOGIN_REQUIRED, then mark the session Expired and ask the user to sign in again. Do not try to rotate __Secure-*PSIDTS.
openQuestions: Does Google in 2026 accept ServiceLogin inside a hand-hosted WebView2 (Edge UA, no spoof) on Windows, or does it show 'This browser or app may not be secure'? Only a live spike can answer this, and the spike means the owner signing in by hand, not an agent.

The InnerTubeX details (ytClient header logic, loginSupported flags per client, player setLogin=true, no Set-Cookie handling) came from WebFetch summaries of HEAD, not a line-by-line read of the v0.7.0 tag Metrolist pins. Should we clone InnerTubeX (GPL-3.0) read-only to confirm exact lines? That needs the owner's OK for another download.

Which exact cookie names does Google set on .youtube.com after ServiceLogin in 2026? (Metrolist only checks SAPISID and stores the whole string, and LOGIN_INFO may be host-scoped to www.youtube.com.) This matters if we filter cookies instead of storing the whole jar.

Does WebView2 Runtime's DBSC (Device Bound Session Credentials), researcher-reported for Edge 147, bind the captured session to the WebView2 profile, so that exported cookies stop working in our own HTTP client after a while?
Is switching brand accounts by only changing onBehalfOfUser (without reloading signinUrl in a window) enough for music.youtube.com browse and www.youtube.com player calls?

Does a signed-in www.youtube.com WEB/WEB_SAFARI player call still get 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot' without a GVS PO token? Metrolist issues #4192 and #4242 report it even while logged in, and the fixes are not visible.

Does the owner accept that streaming with their account risks rate limits or a ban (yt-dlp warning), or should streaming stay anonymous and use the login only as a fallback for age-restricted or LOGIN_REQUIRED videos?

research.findings:
## 0. Where the playback code lives now (Sept 2026)

- Clone: `C:\Users\droid\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\--psf-Home-Desktop-Multiplatform-Music-player\04bbb583-faaf-4a88-9a62-5827ef684e67\scratchpad\Metrolist`. Another agent made it. HEAD is `28fa8f0`, dated 2026-09-23, from https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist.
- `YTPlayerUtils` no longer exists. v13.7.0 "Migrated networking to InnerTubeX with automatic client fallback" (`changelog.md:6`). The app's only entry point for extraction is `app/src/main/kotlin/com/metrolist/music/utils/InnerTubeXPlayer.kt` ("The sole stream extraction entry point", line 34).
- The real logic sits in a separate library: **InnerTubeX v0.7.0**, from JitPack (`gradle/libs.versions.toml:34,103`, `settings.gradle.kts:17-30`). Repo: https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/innertubex. It is **GPL-3.0**, and so is https://github.com/ZemerTeam/zemer-cipher, which it uses. I did not clone InnerTubeX, because only the Metrolist clone was authorised. I read it at tag v0.7.0 through raw.githubusercontent.com, so **InnerTubeX line numbers below are approximate ("~")**. InnerTubeX `main` was pushed 2026-09-25 and may already differ.
- Understand this code, don't copy it: Metrolist, InnerTubeX and zemer-cipher are all GPL-3.0. yt-dlp and yt-dlp/ejs are Unlicense (https://api.github.com/repos/yt-dlp/ejs), and QuickJS is MIT, so those can be reused.

## 1. How the signed-in session gets into the engine

- `app/.../ui/screens/LoginScreen.kt:353-357` opens a WebView on `https://accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin?continue=https%3A%2F%2Fmusic.youtube.com`.
- `LoginScreen.kt:119-179` then polls for up to about 10 s:
  - cookies come from `CookieManager.getCookie("https://music.youtube.com")` (line 124);
  - from page JS it reads `yt.config_.VISITOR_DATA`, `DATASYNC_ID` and `SESSION_INDEX` (lines 139-150);
  - it accepts the login only when a `SAPISID` cookie and visitorData are both present (lines 160-163).
- Those values become `YouTube.cookie`, `visitorData`, `dataSyncId` and `authUser` (lines 183-186).
- It writes cookies back with `Domain=.youtube.com` (line 596).
- **Consequence: one sign-in serves both hosts.** Google's auth cookies (SAPISID and the __Secure-*PSID family) live on `.youtube.com`, so the same jar authenticates music.youtube.com and www.youtube.com. There is no separate "www login".
- `App.kt:182` sets `useLoginForBrowse` to true by default.

## 2. Client catalogue (InnerTubeX `extraction/strategy/PlaybackClientCatalog.kt` ~L77-520, `models/YouTubeClient.kt`)

Clients that are AUTOMATIC in normal playback, with priority, whether they carry the account (`loginSupported`), and their /player host:

| id | priority / lifecycle | account | player host | PO token |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VISIONOS_0_1 | 100, experimental | no | music.youtube.com (`useMusicPlayerEndpoint=true`) | none |
| WEB_REMIX | 70, stable | optional | music.youtube.com | GVS required |
| WEB_EMBEDDED_PLAYER | 65, stable | optional | www.youtube.com (`isEmbedded`) | none |
| WEB_CREATOR | 55 | required | www.youtube.com | GVS required |
| WEB_KIDS | 55 | no | www.youtube.com | none |
| TVHTML5_SIMPLY | 42 | no | music.youtube.com | session + GVS |

- SABR variants (WEB_REMIX_SABR, WEB_SABR, MWEB_SABR, WEB_SAFARI_SABR, TVHTML5_SIMPLY_SABR) are automatic too. **Metrolist turns them off**: `allowHls=false, allowSabr=false` (`InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:71-75`, and line 87 rejects any SABR bootstrap).
- PROBE_ONLY, i.e. not used automatically: ANDROID_VR_* (1.65.10 etc.), TVHTML5_DOWNGRADED (login-capable, www), MWEB.
- Marked BROKEN (priority 0): IOS, ANDROID, ANDROID_MUSIC, TVHTML5, WEB_SAFARI.
- `WEB` is API_ONLY. Its note says "Used for metadata/transcript calls. Playback uses the explicit WEB_SABR profile."
- Client versions match yt-dlp's exactly: WEB 2.20260708.00.00, WEB_REMIX 1.20260707.12.00, ANDROID_VR 1.65.10. InnerTubeX tracks yt-dlp closely.

## 3. Which calls carry the account

InnerTubeX `InnerTube.kt`:
- `ytClient(... includeAccountCookies = true, setLogin = false)`.
- It sends `Cookie` only `if (client.loginSupported && includeAccountCookies)`.
- It adds `X-Goog-AuthUser` and `Authorization: SAPISIDHASH <ts>_<sha1(ts SAPISID origin)>` only `if (setLogin && client.loginSupported && cookie present)` (~L386-400).
- The SAPISID value is taken from `SAPISID`, then `__Secure-3PAPISID`, then `__Secure-1PAPISID` (~L288-299). Only the `SAPISIDHASH` scheme is sent. yt-dlp's `_make_sid_authorization` also sends `SAPISID1PHASH` and `SAPISID3PHASH` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_base.py).
- The player path uses `setLogin = true`. As far as I can tell, **every /player call from a login-capable client (WEB_REMIX, WEB_EMBEDDED_PLAYER, WEB_CREATOR) carries cookies and SAPISIDHASH whenever a session exists. VISIONOS, ANDROID_VR, TVHTML5_SIMPLY and WEB_KIDS are always anonymous.**
- Host selection: WEB_REMIX, or any client with `useMusicPlayerEndpoint`, goes to `https://music.youtube.com/youtubei/v1`; everything else goes to `https://www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1` (~L353-367).
- Browse, next and queue use `setLogin || useLoginForBrowse`; search defaults to login (~L513).
- A `PREF=hl&gl` cookie is injected (~L1428).
- There is a TV `Authorization: Bearer` path (`playerWithTvBearerSessionBound` ~L634; `PlayerClientDirector` ~L302-349). **The Metrolist app never supplies a bearer credential** (`InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:155-168`).

## 4. Extraction order: `InnerTubeExtractor.extractWithDiagnostics` (~L233-375)

1. **Direct stream bypass (~L312-328).** Runs when the track is not video, explicit, age-restricted, uploaded, live, or "authenticated premium high quality".
   - It asks the automatic clients with `allowCipherProcessing=false` and `directAudioOnlyClients=true`, so only responses with ready, decipher-free URLs count.
   - In practice that means **anonymous VISIONOS_0_1 on music.youtube.com**. So **a signed-in Metrolist user still streams ordinary songs anonymously**, which is exactly Monolist's current VISIONOS tier (`Monolist src/innertube.h:196-211`).
2. **Watch-page config (~L336-365).**
   - `cookieFirst = hasSapCookieAuth() && (premiumHQ || isExplicit || isAgeRestricted || isUploaded || wantVideo)`.
   - Calls `extractWithWatchConfig(useLoginCookies = cookieFirst)`. If that fails it retries with the opposite setting: signed-out when cookieFirst was true, authenticated when it was false and a session exists.
   - The config comes from **`https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ID&bpctr=9999999999&has_verified=1`**, with cookies when `useLoginCookies`. What it extracts: PLAYER_JS_URL, STS/signatureTimestamp, INNERTUBE_CLIENT_VERSION and visitorData (`YtConfigParserImpl.kt` ~L22-30, ~L156-192).
   - `useLoginCookies` only affects this page fetch and whether `Cookie` is added to googlevideo media requests (`buildHeaders` ~L1042-1077, allowlisted `*.googlevideo.com/videoplayback` only). It does not strip the cookie from /player calls.
3. **Embedded fallback.** `https://www.youtube.com/embed/ID?html5=1`, with Referer reddit.com, then `/iframe_api`.
4. **Kids fallback** after that.
5. **Client ordering inside each step** (`ContentAwareFallbackStrategy.kt` ~L65-260):
   - Clients are hard-rejected when marked broken, when login is required and there is no session, for uploads without login, or when a PO-token provider or JS runtime is missing.
   - Scoring: start from priority; +25 when the content type is supported; ±18 for auth-optional clients on restricted/uploaded content, depending on signed-in state; −10 experimental, −20 deprecated, −12 per required PO token.
6. **Attempts are sequential**, with a request budget of 2 × the automatic clients (`PlayerClientDirector.kt` ~L39, ~L142-276).
7. **Failed clients are excluded per video for 5 min** (`InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:37,104-130`).
8. The app passes only `isExplicit` and `isUploaded` hints (`MusicService.kt:3832-3835`, `DownloadUtil.kt:124-127`; Cast uses the same at `MusicService.kt:4729`). A playlistId containing `MLPT` also counts as uploaded (`InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:66-70`).

## 5. PO token and visitorData

- visitorData comes from the session. When missing, it is fetched from `https://www.youtube.com/sw.js_data`, with the music homepage as fallback (InnerTube.kt ~L1103-1118; director ~L425-437, 8 s timeout).
- The PO token is minted by the app, not the library. A hidden Android WebView loads BotGuard with base URL `https://www.youtube.com` and calls `https://www.youtube.com/api/jnn/v1/Create` and `/GenerateIT` (`utils/potoken/PoTokenWebView.kt:156,169,210`).
- `PoTokenGenerator.kt:88-156` mints one token bound to the session id (visitorData) once per WebView, then one per videoId. The 8 s timeout (line 80) falls through to token-free clients.
- `InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:189-199` **ignores the `cookie` argument and binds to visitorData even when signed in.**
- yt-dlp's guide says that when logged in, GVS tokens should be bound to the account Session ID (first part of DATASYNC_ID) (https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp-wiki/blob/master/PO%20Token%20Guide.md). So Metrolist's signed-in WEB_REMIX path may be minting mis-bound tokens. **This is my inference; I have not verified it.**
- How the tokens are used:
  - the player token goes into `serviceIntegrityDimensions.poToken` on /player (InnerTube.kt ~L590-606, together with `contentCheckOk`/`racyCheckOk`);
  - the GVS token is appended to the media URL as `&pot=` (Extractor ~L1112-1121);
  - explicit tracks prefetch a token in parallel, with an 18 s cap (~L198-211).
- Per yt-dlp, **Premium accounts do not need a GVS PO token** (https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/PO-Token-Guide, edited 2026-07-12). InnerTubeX models this as `premiumMayBypass` in `PoTokenRule` (`PlaybackClientManifest.kt` ~L67).

## 6. Signature and n deciphering

- `cipher/YouTubeCipherService.kt` (~L280-450) solves `s`/`sp` and `n` in this order:
  1. remote per-player-version configs: zemer-cipher JSON from `raw.githubusercontent.com/ZemerTeam/zemer-cipher/.../player_configs.json` (`InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:264-265`);
  2. a GitHub legacy config;
  3. **yt-dlp-ejs solver scripts run in QuickJS** (resources `yt_ejs/yt.solver.core.min.js` and `yt.solver.lib.min.js`);
  4. a regex parser of base.js.
- base.js is downloaded from `/s/player/.../base.js` and kept in a 4-entry LRU cache.
- `refreshAfterStreamRejection()` refreshes configs after the CDN rejects a deciphered URL (~L154). The app calls it on 403/410 (`MusicService.kt:3275-3320`).
- A VISIONOS answer needs none of this, which is why it is the fast path.

## 7. Format choice

- `extraction/FormatSelectors.kt` pins **no itags** (no 141/774/251 constants).
  - LOW: smallest audio/mp4.
  - AUTO: best audio/webm (Opus) by score.
  - HIGH: highest bitrate, then channels, sample rate and container.
  - AUTO falls back to LOW on metered networks (`InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:282-292`).
- Premium 256 kbps (141 AAC / 774 Opus) would only be reached through `ContentHints.premium`, which the library says must be set "only when the caller has independently confirmed YouTube Premium". **Metrolist never sets it**: grep finds no "premium" anywhere in `app/src/main/kotlin` or `innertube/`.
- On the yt-dlp side, premium formats have been missing even with Premium cookies since 2025.08. See https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14208 (open) and https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17729 (opened 2026-09-24, open).
- yt-dlp master still has `_DEFAULT_PREMIUM_CLIENTS = ('web_creator','tv_downgraded','web')` with the comment "Premium does not require POT" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_video.py). **Treat Premium-quality audio as currently unreliable for any third-party client.**

## 8. LOGIN_REQUIRED, age-restricted and bot checks

- `extraction/PlayabilityFailure.kt` (~L20-45):
  - AGE_CHECK_REQUIRED, AGE_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED, CONTENT_CHECK_REQUIRED, and reasons such as "confirm your age" or "age-restricted" map to `AGE_RESTRICTED`;
  - "video unavailable", "private video" and similar map to `UNAVAILABLE`;
  - **`LOGIN_REQUIRED` is classed as a TOKEN failure**, so the director moves on to tokenized or other clients. That is how "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" (which arrives as LOGIN_REQUIRED) gets handled.
  - There is no special matching on the bot string.
  - A response counts as playable only with status `OK` plus a usable audio format or HLS URL (`PlayerClientDirector.kt` ~L508-511).
- App side:
  - 403/410 from the CDN means an expired URL: the client is marked failed, caches are cleared and the track is retried (`MusicService.kt:2915-2920, 3056, 3275-3320`);
  - the UI shows "Explicit playback works better with a logged-in account." for age / LOGIN_REQUIRED / 403 errors (`ui/player/PlaybackError.kt:64-80`; `res/values/metrolist_strings.xml:536`).

## 9. Playback tracking (history → recommendations)

- `InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:328-336` keeps only `videostatsPlaybackUrl` and `videostatsWatchtimeUrl` (`atrUrl = null`). The extractor drops tracking for TV-bearer results (~L691).
- `MusicService.kt:4036-4075`: once a play reaches `HistoryDuration` (default 30 s, line 4041), the app calls `YouTube.registerPlayback(null, playbackUrl)`.
  - Only the *playback* ping is sent; watchtime pings are never sent.
  - The ping is **not** gated by `PauseListenHistoryKey`, which only gates the local DB (lines 4043-4044 vs 4061).
- `innertube/.../InnerTube.kt:207-212` sends that ping as client **WEB_REMIX**. InnerTubeX `registerStatsWithSession` attaches Cookie, X-Goog-AuthUser and SAPISIDHASH for login-capable clients. Params are `ver=2`, `c`, `cpn` and `final`. Hosts are restricted to s.youtube.com, www.youtube.com and music.youtube.com, paths to `/api/stats/playback|watchtime` (~L803-843).
- So even though the stream was fetched anonymously (VISIONOS), **the listen is reported to the signed-in account's history**. That is what personalises the YouTube Music feed.
- The cpn is a random 16-char string (`YouTube.kt:2912-2931`).

## 10. What signing in unlocks, compared with anonymous

- **Access:**
  - explicit/age-gated tracks (cookie-first plus the +18 score);
  - private and uploaded (MLPT) tracks, since "uploads require login" hard-rejects signed-out clients;
  - WEB_CREATOR, which requires login.
- **Robustness:** fewer bot checks and higher limits. The yt-dlp wiki gives about 300 videos/h for a guest against about 2000 videos/h with an account, and warns the account "risk[s] being banned" (https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors).
- **History reporting** to the account, which is the main feed benefit (§9).
- **Premium:**
  - no GVS PO token needed;
  - in theory 141/774, but not wired up in Metrolist and currently broken upstream (§7).
- **Not unlocked:** different "real" files. For a non-Premium account, the googlevideo `/videoplayback` files are the same whether an anonymous VISIONOS call or a signed-in web call asked for them.

## 11. What "use the login on www.youtube.com to get the real files" means for a desktop app today

1. **The website's own path is SABR.** The `WEB` client on www.youtube.com now returns only SABR formats (no plain URLs). It needs a GVS PO token from BotGuard unless the account is Premium, plus base.js sig/n solving (https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12482, PO Token Guide). Copying it for real means three things:
   - a SABR/UMP client (InnerTubeX has one under `sabr/`, but Metrolist itself disables it);
   - a DOM-capable JS runtime for BotGuard. **Qt WebEngine "does not compile with MinGW"** (https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtwebengine-platform-notes.html), so on our toolchain that means WebView2 or a helper process;
   - a sig/n solver.

   That is heavy and brittle, and no mature client does this for ordinary audio.
2. **The practical meaning is what yt-dlp does with cookies in 2026.**
   - `_DEFAULT_CLIENTS = ('visionos','web')`, `_DEFAULT_AUTHED_CLIENTS = ('web_embedded','tv_downgraded','web')` (yt-dlp `_video.py`).
   - All the authed clients call **www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/player with the .youtube.com cookies and SAPISIDHASH**.
   - `web_embedded` and `tv_downgraded` return ordinary https formats that need sig/n solving through a JS runtime (deno + yt-dlp-ejs). Monolist already ships this: `src/ytdlp.cpp:449-451`.
   - **So Monolist can "stream through www.youtube.com with the login" by giving yt-dlp the session's cookies (`--cookies <netscape file>`) on a dedicated rung**, and yt-dlp picks the authed clients itself.
   - Caveats:
     - the file holds secrets: create it in a private directory, delete it afterwards, and never log it;
     - yt-dlp writes the cookie jar back into that file, so read it back to capture rotated cookies for YtmSession;
     - there is account-ban risk, so keep the call rate low.
3. **Native later.** Add an authed `TVHTML5_DOWNGRADED` or `WEB_EMBEDDED_PLAYER` request to our own InnerTube on www.youtube.com, with Cookie + SAPISIDHASH (add the 1P/3P variants like yt-dlp) + signatureTimestamp. Solve sig/n with an embedded QuickJS (MIT, MinGW-friendly) running yt-dlp-ejs (Unlicense). This is the same architecture as InnerTubeX, written by us.
4. **Suggested Monolist ladder, mirroring Metrolist's behaviour:**
   - keep the anonymous VISIONOS tier first for ordinary tracks;
   - go to the signed-in www.youtube.com rung only when:
     - the track is explicit, age-restricted, private or uploaded;
     - the anonymous tier answers LOGIN_REQUIRED, a bot check, or AGE_*;
     - or the user opts in;
   - keep the yt-dlp anonymous / muxed / Piped tiers below it.
   - Add signed-in videostats *playback* pings, with an off switch, so listens feed YouTube Music recommendations. This fits the owner's "login for the feed", costs little, and is how Metrolist actually improves its feed.
   - Don't chase 141/774 or SABR for now.

## Monolist (read-only) context checked

- `src/innertube.h:193-211`: Client {Music, YouTube, Player}. "Only the Music client ever carries the account: playback (Player), youtube.com's search and yt-dlp never do."
- `src/streamresolver.h:44-57`: tiers are InnerTube, YtDlp, Muxed, Piped, Invidious.
- `src/ytdlp.cpp:489-500`: `resolveAudio` passes no cookies.
- `src/ytdlp.cpp:515`: the muxed tier uses `player_client=android,tv_simply`.

research.recommendation:
Don't try to copy the www.youtube.com website's own playback (SABR, BotGuard PO tokens and SAPISIDHASH on the WEB client). Metrolist doesn't do it either. Even signed in, it streams ordinary songs through the anonymous VISIONOS client, which is the same as Monolist's current fast tier. It uses the account only for three things: restricted or uploaded tracks, the fallback clients that accept cookies, and reporting each listen to the account's history. That last one is what makes the feed personal.

For Monolist:
1. Keep VISIONOS anonymous as tier 0.
2. Add one signed-in www.youtube.com rung. It runs only for explicit, age-restricted, private or uploaded tracks, when the anonymous tier returns LOGIN_REQUIRED, a bot check or an age check, or when the user opts in.
   - First version: pass YtmSession's .youtube.com cookies to the yt-dlp tier we already have (`--cookies`, with deno and ejs). yt-dlp then picks its signed-in clients itself (web_embedded, tv_downgraded, web). Write the cookie file to a private temp location, read it back afterwards to pick up rotated cookies, delete it, and never log it.
   - Later: a native signed-in TVHTML5_DOWNGRADED or WEB_EMBEDDED_PLAYER call to www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/player. It would send the cookies plus all three SAPISIDHASH variants and solve the signature and n parameters with an embedded QuickJS running the yt-dlp-ejs scripts. We would write it ourselves; Metrolist, InnerTubeX and zemer-cipher are GPL-3.0, so their code is off-limits.
3. Add signed-in playback pings (the videostats playback URL, sent with cookies, after about 30 s of listening), with a "pause YouTube history" switch. This is the cheap, high-value part of "use the login for the feed".
4. Don't build the Premium 141/774 formats or SABR yet. Premium formats have been broken in yt-dlp since 2025-08, and SABR needs BotGuard plus UMP.
5. The in-app sign-in window can't use Qt WebEngine, because it doesn't build with MinGW. It needs WebView2 or a helper process; the login research should cover that.

research.findings:
## 1. Short answer

**Building it: yes.** A Qt 6.11 app built with MinGW 13.1 can open an Edge WebView2 sign-in window and read every cookie from it, HttpOnly ones included. It needs no MSVC, no QtWebEngine and no WRL. There are two catches:

- Qt's own WebView2 plugin is MSVC-only, and it does not expose cookie values. So we write a thin WebView2 host ourselves, roughly 500–800 lines of C++.
- Whether Google lets people sign in inside WebView2 in 2026 is **uncertain**. Google's official policy says embedded browsers are blocked. In practice, several embedded engines do sign in today, but the evidence for WebView2 specifically is mixed. A short probe, with the owner signing in himself, has to settle it before we commit.

## 2. How Metrolist does it (GPL-3.0, read only to understand it)

Clone: `scratchpad\Metrolist`, commit `28fa8f04`, dated 2026-09-23. All paths below are under `app\src\main\kotlin\com\metrolist\music\`.

- **Sign-in page.** `ui\screens\LoginScreen.kt:305-359` creates a plain `android.webkit.WebView` with JavaScript and DOM storage on (`:341-347`). It loads `https://accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin?continue=https%3A%2F%2Fmusic.youtube.com` (`:357`).
- **No custom user agent at login.** The only user-agent override in the app is in `utils\potoken\PoTokenWebView.kt:76`, which has nothing to do with sign-in.
- **Detecting success.** `onPageFinished` on host `music.youtube.com` (`:331-339`) starts extraction.
- **Reading the session** (`:119-179`):
  - the cookie string comes from `CookieManager.getInstance().getCookie("https://music.youtube.com")` (`:124`), a native API that includes HttpOnly cookies;
  - `yt.config_.VISITOR_DATA`, `DATASYNC_ID` and `SESSION_INDEX` are read by JavaScript (`:139-150`);
  - it requires the `SAPISID` cookie to be present (`:160`) and retries 20 times at 500 ms.
- **Channel picker.** `YouTube.accountsList()` handles brand/channel accounts (`:233-266`, `:390-457`).
- **Validate and save.** It checks the session with `YouTube.accountInfo()` (`:189`), saves it to DataStore (`:192-200`), clears the WebView cache and history (`:204-210`), then restarts the app (`:212-217`).
- **Sign-out.** `App.kt:331-370` removes the DataStore keys and calls `CookieManager.removeAllCookies`.

**WebView2 equivalents for each step:**

| Metrolist (Android) | WebView2 |
|---|---|
| `loadUrl` | `ICoreWebView2::Navigate` |
| `onPageFinished` | `add_NavigationCompleted` + `get_Source` |
| JavaScript bridge | `ExecuteScript("JSON.stringify({...ytcfg})")`, which returns JSON |
| `CookieManager.getCookie` | `ICoreWebView2_2::get_CookieManager` → `GetCookies(L"https://music.youtube.com")` and `GetCookies(L"https://www.youtube.com")` |
| `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` | `add_NavigationStarting` / `add_NewWindowRequested` |
| `removeAllCookies` | `DeleteAllCookies` or `ClearBrowsingDataAll` |

A Compose-Desktop port of Metrolist, Lyrenne (GPL-3.0, pushed 2026-09-18), took a different route on Windows. Its `desktop\...\auth\BrowserLoginHelper.kt` launches the system **Edge/Chrome/Brave** with a temporary `--user-data-dir` and opens `https://music.youtube.com`. After the user closes the browser, it reads the profile's Cookies SQLite database with DPAPI. Its comment says a fresh profile still writes v10 cookies that decrypt fine, while the app-bound "v20" encryption on normal profiles cannot be read. Its 2.11.1 release notes mention constant cookie rotation, which `AuthManager.kt:127-143` handles by merging Set-Cookie headers. ([repo](https://github.com/Doctordefector/Metrolist-Desktop))

## 3. Hosting WebView2 from MinGW

### Runtime
- Microsoft says the Evergreen runtime is part of Windows 11 and is on "the vast majority" of Windows 10 devices. Apps should still check for it: registry `pv` under `...\EdgeUpdate\Clients\{F3017226-FE2A-4295-8BDF-00C3A9A7E4C5}`, or `GetAvailableCoreWebView2BrowserVersionString`. The fallback is the roughly 2 MB bootstrapper. ([distribution docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/distribution))
- **Checked on this ARM64 VM:** runtime `153.0.4234.48` is installed in `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\EdgeWebView\Application\153.0.4234.48`. Its `EBWebView` folder has `arm64`, `x64` and `x86` subfolders, so our x64-under-emulation build has an x64 client DLL to load. Not yet tested at runtime.

### SDK and licence
- NuGet `Microsoft.Web.WebView2` 1.0.4191.47 (2026-08-28) has a **BSD-3-style licence** ([licence](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Web.WebView2/1.0.4191.47/License)). That fits our MIT project; we just keep the notice.
- It supplies `WebView2.h`, `WebView2EnvironmentOptions.h` and `WebView2Loader.dll`.

### Headers and loader under MinGW
- MSYS2 ships the NuGet headers and DLL **unpatched** for mingw-w64 ([PKGBUILD](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/msys2/MINGW-packages/master/mingw-w64-webview2-loader/PKGBUILD), [package](https://packages.msys2.org/packages/mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-webview2-loader)). That package is the dependency of MSYS2's `webview` build.
- `WebView2LoaderStatic.lib` is MSVC-only. The webview README says static linking "is possible with Visual C++ but not MinGW-w64" ([webview/webview](https://github.com/webview/webview)).
- So on MinGW we either ship `WebView2Loader.dll` and call `CreateCoreWebView2EnvironmentWithOptions` through LoadLibrary/GetProcAddress, or reimplement the loader.
  - webview (MIT) does the latter. Its `core/include/webview/detail/platform/windows/webview2/loader.hh` reads `EdgeUpdate\ClientState\{F3017226...}`, loads `EBWebView\<arch>\EmbeddedBrowserWebView.dll` and calls the undocumented export `CreateWebViewEnvironmentWithOptionsInternal`. That is fragile, so shipping Microsoft's DLL is the better choice.

### Our toolchain
- Checked: the Qt MinGW 13.1 kit (mingw-w64 headers v11) has `eventtoken.h`, which `WebView2.h` needs, and `wrl/client.h` (ComPtr).
- It has **no** `wrl/implements.h` or `wrl/event.h`, so WRL's `Callback`/`Make` are unavailable.

### COM without WRL
- We write small handler classes that implement `QueryInterface`, `AddRef`, `Release` and `Invoke`, for example one template around `std::function`.
- IIDs: webview defines them as `constexpr IID` literals and matches them with `cast_if_equal_iid` (`loader.hh` and `backends/win32_edge.hh`). GCC's `__uuidof` only works with `__CRT_UUID_DECL`, so plan on defining the few IIDs we need. Confirm this in the probe.

### Threading
- WebView2 needs a single-threaded (STA) UI thread with a message pump.
- Qt's Windows plugin already calls `OleInitialize(nullptr)` in the `QWindowsContextPrivate` constructor ([qwindowscontext.cpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt/qtbase/dev/src/plugins/platforms/windows/qwindowscontext.cpp)), and Qt's Win32 event loop delivers WebView2's callbacks. We must never block the GUI thread waiting on them; use a QTimer or state machine instead of Metrolist's retry loop.

### Where the window lives
- Use a **separate top-level window**: a plain `QWindow` or a `CreateWindowExW` window, owned by the main window's `winId()`.
- Create the controller on that HWND and call `put_Bounds` on resize. Call `Controller->Close()` before quitting.
- Do not overlay it on the QQuickWindow. Qt's own docs say "overlapping the WebView with other QML components is not supported" ([Qt WebView](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtwebview-index.html)).

### What does not work
- **Qt WebView's WebView2 backend** (new in Qt 6.10; [Qt 6.10 release](https://www.qt.io/blog/qt-6.10-released)) is built only when `WIN32 AND MSVC AND WebView2_FOUND` (`src/webview/configure.cmake`). It uses `Microsoft::WRL::Callback` (`src/plugins/windows/qwebview2webview.cpp`). Its API only reports `cookieAdded(domain, name)`, with no values, and only for cookies set through `setCookie` ([WebView QML type](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qml-qtwebview-webview.html)). Our kit ships no WebView module at all (checked `plugins`).
- **webview/webview** (MIT) builds with MinGW but hard-codes its data folder to `%APPDATA%\<exe name>` (`win32_edge.hh` ~1056-1066) and has no cookie or user-agent API. It only helps as a reference, or through `webview_get_native_handle(..., WEBVIEW_NATIVE_HANDLE_KIND_BROWSER_CONTROLLER)`, which returns the `ICoreWebView2Controller*`.

## 4. Cookies, private profile, sign-out

- **Reading cookies.** `ICoreWebView2CookieManager::GetCookies(uri, handler)` has existed since SDK 1.0.705.50. An empty URI returns every cookie in the profile. Each `ICoreWebView2Cookie` exposes `get_Name`, `get_Value`, `get_Domain`, `get_IsHttpOnly`, `get_IsSecure`, `get_Expires`, and so on ([cookie manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/reference/win32/icorewebview2cookiemanager), [cookie](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/reference/win32/icorewebview2cookie)). HttpOnly cookies come back because this is a host-side API. One sign-in covers both hosts, since the auth cookies live on `.youtube.com`. Kaset reuses one login for music and www, with a separate SAPISIDHASH origin for each (ADR-0020, below).
- **Private profile.** Pass our own `userDataFolder` to `CreateCoreWebView2EnvironmentWithOptions`. WebView2 never uses the user's Edge profile. The docs say to prefer a custom folder and to avoid network drives ([user data folder](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/user-data-folder)). So it must go under `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, never the `\\psf` share.
  - Option: `ICoreWebView2ControllerOptions::IsInPrivateModeEnabled` keeps nothing on disk ([multi-profile](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/multi-profile-support), not re-read this session). The cost is a blank profile on every sign-in, which Lyrenne 2.11.1 says makes sign-in harder.
- **Sign-out.**
  - Use `ICoreWebView2Profile2::ClearBrowsingDataAll()` or `ClearBrowsingData(kinds)`, or `CookieManager::DeleteAllCookies` ([clear browsing data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/clear-browsing-data)).
  - To delete the whole folder, first end the session and wait for the browser process to exit (`BrowserProcessId`, BrowserProcessExited); files can stay locked until then.
  - Also wipe our DPAPI-stored cookie copy.
- **Settings for the sign-in view:**
  - DevTools off;
  - `IsPasswordAutosaveEnabled` and `IsGeneralAutofillEnabled` off;
  - no host objects;
  - only run `ExecuteScript` once the page is on `music.youtube.com` or `www.youtube.com`. Never script `accounts.google.com`.
- **Keeping the session alive.** YouTube rotates account cookies on open YouTube tabs. yt-dlp's advice is to sign in, take the cookies, and never reopen that session in a browser ([yt-dlp wiki](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors)). The same wiki warns of account bans when using yt-dlp.
  - So we read the cookies, then close the sign-in view and never keep YouTube open in it.
  - Afterwards, merge Set-Cookie headers from our own requests back into the store, as Lyrenne's `AuthManager.kt:127-143` does.

## 5. Does Google allow sign-in inside WebView2 (2025–2026)?

**Official policy is against it.**
- Google says sign-in is blocked from browsers that "are embedded in a different application" or "controlled through software automation" ([Google support](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/7675428)).
- Google's 2020 blog said "Google Account sign-ins from all embedded frameworks will be blocked" from 2021-01-04 ([Google Developers blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/guidance-to-developers-affected-by-our-effort-to-block-less-secure-browsers-and-applications/)).
- OAuth in webviews is banned outright ([Google Developers blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/upcoming-security-changes-to-googles-oauth-20-authorization-endpoint-in-embedded-webviews/)). Microsoft said "google auth flows will not be supported in WebView2" ([#1647](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/1647)). That concerns OAuth; we would use the normal web sign-in page, like Metrolist.

**Enforcement in practice is heuristic:**

| Engine / app | Result | Date |
|---|---|---|
| Android WebView, default UA (Metrolist) | Ships and works | 2026-09 |
| Electron: honest UA vs spoofed plain Chrome UA ([traycer PR #1889](https://github.com/traycerai/traycer/pull/1889)) | Spoofed Chrome UA rejected as "not secure" because Electron's JavaScript environment doesn't match real Chrome; honest Electron UA "not rejected" | 2026-09-14 |
| Pear Desktop / th-ch (Electron) ([src/index.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pear-devs/pear-desktop/master/src/index.ts)) | Uses a spoofed Chrome 130 UA for browsing but **restores the original UA** for `accounts.google.com` requests | current source; fix dates from 2021 ([PR #515](https://github.com/th-ch/youtube-music/pull/515)) |
| WKWebView (Kaset, MIT) | Works with a Safari 17 UA (`WebKitManager.swift` ~l.89) plus a script that hides passkeys, because Google's passkey flow dead-ends in WKWebView ([ADR-0033](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sozercan/kaset/main/docs/adr/0033-login-passkey-suppression.md)) | 2026 |
| WebView2 (ytm-tauri, MIT, Windows-only) ([repo](https://github.com/xzelleiv/ytm-tauri)) | Sets a Chrome/131 UA (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs` ~l.18, 210); claims persistent YouTube login; PR #1 "fixes regional Google sign-in" | 2026-08/09 |
| WebView2 and WKWebView under Tauri ([clpanic.com](https://clpanic.com/youtube-music-3mb/)) | "Google refuses to log you in"; fixed with a Chrome UA **plus** spoofing `window.chrome`, `navigator.userAgentData`, `plugins` and `webdriver` on every origin | undated, likely 2026 |
| WebView2 in WebView2Feedback [#1578](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/1578), [#1584](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/1584), [#2552](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/2552) | "This browser or app may not be secure"; #2552 closed as stale in 2024 as "likely not relevant to newer runtimes" | 2021–2022 |
| Pake / Tauri docs issue ([#1148](https://github.com/tw93/pake/issues/1148)) | Google sign-in not reliable in system webviews | 2026-03 |

**Why WebView2 is easy for Google to spot.** WebView2 announces itself: `navigator.userAgentData.brands` includes `"Microsoft Edge WebView2"` ([#2576](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/2576)). Setting `put_UserAgent` "may clear User Agent Client Hints headers Sec-CH-UA-* and script values from navigator.userAgentData" ([Settings2 docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/reference/win32/icorewebview2settings2)). That mismatch is exactly the kind the traycer PR says Google punishes.

**Conclusion:** likely to work, but not guaranteed, and Google can switch it off without notice. The probe should test in this order:
1. the default, honest WebView2 user agent;
2. a plain Edge/Chrome UA;
3. passkey suppression through `AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated`, only if the passkey dead-end appears.

## 6. Fallback when WebView2 is refused

Use Lyrenne's approach: launch the **real system Edge**, which is present on Windows 10/11, with a temporary `--user-data-dir` and `--no-first-run`. Google has no reason to block it. Read cookies after the user closes the window.
- Reading the Cookies file means DPAPI and AES-GCM decryption; Lyrenne says fresh profiles still write v10 cookies.
- Or read them live over Chrome's remote-debugging protocol (`--remote-debugging-port` with a non-default profile).
- Both are **uncertain**: v20 encryption or automation detection could reach them. Our existing cookie import stays as the last resort.

## 7. macOS and Linux (for the other sessions)

- **macOS:** WKWebView in a native NSWindow/NSPanel from Objective-C++, not Qt WebView, because Qt WebView gives no cookie values.
  - Storage: `WKWebsiteDataStore.nonPersistent()`, or `dataStoreForIdentifier:` (macOS 14+) for a private persistent store.
  - Cookies: `httpCookieStore.getAllCookies` returns NSHTTPCookie objects, HttpOnly included. Kaset reads SAPISID and checks `__Secure-3PAPISID` ([architecture.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sozercan/kaset/main/docs/architecture.md)).
  - Set a Safari UA and suppress passkeys (Kaset `LoginPasskeySuppression.swift`).
  - Sign-out: `removeDataOfTypes` or remove the identified store.
- **Linux:** WebKitGTK. `webkit_cookie_manager_get_all_cookies` (2.42+) returns SoupCookie objects ([WebKitGTK CookieManager](https://webkitgtk.org/reference/webkit2gtk/stable/class.CookieManager.html)).
  - Mixing a GTK main loop into a Qt process is awkward, so a small helper process is better.
  - This is the weakest platform for Google sign-in. GNOME Online Accounts removed its embedded WebKitGTK browser in 3.49 and now hands sign-in to the default browser ([GNOME issue](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gnome-online-accounts/-/issues/222)). Expect to need the system-browser or cookie-import fallback there.

## 8. Licences

- **Can reuse, with the notice:** WebView2 SDK and loader (BSD-3), webview/webview (MIT), Kaset (MIT), ytm-tauri (MIT), Pear Desktop (MIT).
- **Ideas only, no code copying:** Metrolist and Lyrenne (GPL-3.0).

## (b) A signed-in www.youtube.com streaming tier

**Facts that decide the client:**

- **VISIONOS cannot carry the account.**
  - yt-dlp: in `_base.py`, `visionos` has no `SUPPORTS_COOKIES`, while `web`, `web_safari`, `web_embedded`, `tv`/`tv_downgraded`, `web_music` and `mweb` do ([_base.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_base.py)).
  - With cookies, yt-dlp skips clients that cannot take them and warns: *Skipping client "android" since it does not support cookies* ([louis#16](https://github.com/stuartromanek/louis/issues/16), 25 Aug 2026).
  - InnerTubeX's `PlaybackClientCatalog.kt` marks VISIONOS and ANDROID_VR as authentication UNSUPPORTED ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MetrolistGroup/innertubex/main/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/metrolist/innertubex/extraction/strategy/PlaybackClientCatalog.kt); from a WebFetch summary, about lines 107-199).
- **Which clients do carry the account:**
  - yt-dlp uses `_DEFAULT_AUTHED_CLIENTS = ('web_embedded', 'tv_downgraded', 'web')` and `_DEFAULT_PREMIUM_CLIENTS = ('web_creator', 'tv_downgraded', 'web')` ([_video.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_video.py)).
  - `web` needs a GVS PO token; tv and web_embedded have no PO-token policy; all of them need the JS player (signature and n).
  - InnerTubeX agrees: TVHTML5_DOWNGRADED and WEB_EMBEDDED_PLAYER are authentication OPTIONAL with no PO token, and WEB_REMIX is OPTIONAL but needs a GVS PO token.
- **Metrolist itself keeps anonymous VISIONOS first for ordinary songs.** InnerTubeX's `ContentAwareFallbackStrategy.kt` does two things:
  - It pushes auth-UNSUPPORTED clients down only when `request.authenticated && ((premiumHighQuality && request.premium) || request.hints.wantVideo)`.
  - It gives OPTIONAL-auth clients a `+18 "authenticated"` boost only for `restrictedContent`, meaning explicit, kids, age-restricted or uploaded content (verbatim via WebFetch, about lines 60-95 and 237-245 on `main`).
  - Metrolist's app feeds `isUploaded` and disallows SABR and HLS (`app/.../utils/InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:65-75`).
- **Monolist cannot use any cookie-capable client in-process today.** It has no signature or n-parameter solver in the app; `player()` deliberately passes over `signatureCipher` formats (`src/innertube.cpp:979-983`). yt-dlp already has Deno wired in (`src/ytdlp.cpp:449-451`).

**Can yt-dlp take cookies? Yes.**
- `--cookies FILE`: "Netscape formatted file to read cookies from and dump cookie jar in". It **writes the jar back** to that file.
- `--cookies-from-browser BROWSER[+KEYRING][:PROFILE][::CONTAINER]` ([README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/README.md)). Avoid it here: Chrome and Edge app-bound encryption blocks it on Windows (yt-dlp #10927, per `CONNECTIONS_DESIGN.md:155`), and it would share the live main-browser session.

design.howMetrolistDoesIt:
Source: shallow clone of https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist (GPL-3.0), HEAD 28fa8f0, 2026-09-23. It is at C:\Users\droid\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\--psf-Home-Desktop-Multiplatform-Music-player\04bbb583-faaf-4a88-9a62-5827ef684e67\scratchpad\Metrolist, and the paths below are relative to it. I read it to understand the mechanism only; no code is to be copied. Since v13.7.0, networking lives in a separate GPL-3.0 library, InnerTubeX v0.7.0 (gradle/libs.versions.toml:34; changelog.md:6; https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/InnerTubeX). The researchers read InnerTubeX through web fetches, so its line numbers are approximate (~).

SIGN-IN (verified by me in app/src/main/kotlin/com/metrolist/music/ui/screens/LoginScreen.kt)
- It is a plain Android WebView with only JavaScript and DOM storage turned on. It sets no custom user agent and has no special flags (L341-347).
- It loads https://accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin?continue=https%3A%2F%2Fmusic.youtube.com (L353-359). This is Google's normal web sign-in page, not OAuth. The user types their own password and completes 2FA.
- Only http and https stay in the view. intent: links go to an external app, and every other scheme is swallowed (L311-329). That fixes https://github.com/MetrolistGroup/Metrolist/issues/3183.
- Success trigger: onPageFinished on a page whose host is exactly music.youtube.com (L331-339).
- It then polls 20 times. Each round waits up to 1 s for a JS answer, then 500 ms, so roughly 10-30 s in total (L119-179). The researcher who wrote "about 10 s" was slightly off.
  - Cookies come from the native CookieManager.getCookie("https://music.youtube.com") (L124). That includes HttpOnly and .youtube.com cookies, but not .google.com.
  - Page script reads window.yt.config_.VISITOR_DATA, DATASYNC_ID and SESSION_INDEX (L139-150).
  - It accepts the session only when a SAPISID cookie and a non-blank VISITOR_DATA are both present (L160-169).
  - It keeps DATASYNC_ID up to '||', and SESSION_INDEX as authUser (L167-168).
- Validation and saving (L181-218):
  - YouTube.accountInfo() calls account/account_menu on the music client.
  - The cookie string, visitorData, dataSyncId, authUser and name/email/handle are saved in a plain, unencrypted DataStore.
  - It then clears the WebView cache and history and restarts the whole process.
- Brand channels (L233-266, L390-457):
  - account/accounts_list is called on the WEB client at www.youtube.com.
  - If there is more than one channel, a picker loads the chosen channel's signinUrl in the same WebView, re-captures, and uses that channel's datasyncIdToken.
- Sign-out: App.kt:331-370 removes the keys and calls CookieManager.removeAllCookies. Nothing is revoked on Google's side.
- Expiry: there is no expiry or refresh detection. "Logged in" just means SAPISID is present (utils/SyncUtils.kt:271-281).
- There is also a manual "Log in with token" paste (AccountSettings.kt:188-253). That is the same idea as our existing cookie import.

ONE JAR, BOTH HOSTS
- Google's session cookies (SAPISID, the SID family, the __Secure-1P/3P* family) are set on Domain=.youtube.com. The one jar captured on music.youtube.com is therefore sent both to music.youtube.com (WEB_REMIX: browse/feed) and to www.youtube.com (WEB: accounts_list, player clients).
- The Authorization SAPISIDHASH is computed with the origin of whichever host is being called (InnerTubeX InnerTube.kt ytClient, ~L353-400).
- There is no separate "www login".

STREAMING WHILE SIGNED IN (verified in app/.../utils/InnerTubeXPlayer.kt and playback/MusicService.kt; InnerTubeX details approximate)
- Metrolist does NOT stream ordinary songs with the account.
  - Its first attempt is a "direct stream" bypass that takes decipher-free URLs from the anonymous VISIONOS client. InnerTubeX marks VISIONOS as unable to carry cookies (InnerTubeExtractor ~L312-328; PlaybackClientCatalog).
  - The account is used "cookie-first" only for explicit, age-restricted, uploaded (MLPT) or video content. It is also used on the fallback clients that accept cookies: WEB_REMIX, WEB_EMBEDDED_PLAYER and WEB_CREATOR.
  - HLS and SABR are switched off (InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:65-75).
  - PO tokens come from a hidden BotGuard WebView, bound to visitorData even when signed in (InnerTubeXPlayer.kt:191-199).
- The account's real effect on the feed is the listen ping.
  - After 30 s of listening, MusicService.kt:4061-4074 calls YouTube.registerPlayback on the player response's videostatsPlaybackUrl.
  - That call goes as WEB_REMIX with the account (innertube/.../InnerTube.kt:207-212).
  - It is NOT gated by the "pause listen history" switch, which only gates the local database (L4043-4044).
  - This is how Metrolist's YouTube Music Home learns what you play.
- Cross-check with yt-dlp master (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_video.py and _base.py, fetched today):
  - _DEFAULT_AUTHED_CLIENTS = ('web_embedded','tv_downgraded','web').
  - visionos has SUPPORTS_COOKIES=False.
  - web_embedded and tv_downgraded accept cookies, post to www.youtube.com, have no GVS PO-token policy, and need the JS player.
  - web needs a GVS PO token for https/DASH formats unless the account is Premium.
  - The auth header carries SAPISIDHASH, SAPISID1PHASH and SAPISID3PHASH.
  - DATASYNC_ID is "DELEGATED_SESSION_ID||USER_SESSION_ID" for a brand channel, or "USER_SESSION_ID||" otherwise.
  - X-Goog-AuthUser is SESSION_INDEX.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR US
- The owner's picture is right: one sign-in, the YouTube Music side for the feed, www.youtube.com for signed-in streaming.
- For a non-Premium account, though, the "real files" are the same googlevideo /videoplayback files that our anonymous tier already gets. Monolist's VISIONOS tier already posts to https://www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/player (src/innertube.cpp:762, 780).
- What the account adds:
  - access to age-gated, "confirm you're not a bot" and private or uploaded tracks;
  - higher rate limits (yt-dlp wiki: about 300 videos/h as a guest vs about 2000/h with an account, https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors);
  - listens counted toward the feed.
design.signInDesign:
GOAL
A "Sign in with Google" button that opens an in-app window, like Metrolist's. The owner signs in himself; Monolist reads the session from the window and hands it to the existing YtmSession. The cookie file/paste import stays exactly as it is, as the fallback.

ARCHITECTURE (our own code, MIT)
1. src/signin/signinflow.{h,cpp}: a platform-neutral QObject state machine.
   - States: Idle, Opening, WaitingForUser, Capturing, Validating, Done, and Failed(reason). Failed reasons: Refused, NoRuntime, Timeout, Cancelled, NotSignedIn.
   - It talks to a small backend interface:
     - open(url, profileDir)
     - navigated(url, ok)
     - runScript(js)
     - cookies(urls)
     - close() → closed()
2. src/signin/signinbackend_webview2.cpp (Windows, now): a hand-hosted Edge WebView2.
   - We don't use Qt WebEngine: it does not build with MinGW (https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtwebengine-platform-notes.html).
   - We don't use Qt WebView: its WebView2 backend is gated on MSVC and exposes no cookie values (qtwebview configure.cmake; https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qml-qtwebview-webview.html).
   - We don't use webview/webview: it has no data-folder or cookie API.
   - Its details are under "WINDOWS WEBVIEW2 HOST".
3. macOS backend (the other session): WKWebView in an NSPanel from Objective-C++.
4. Linux backend (later): a WebKitGTK helper process.

WINDOWS WEBVIEW2 HOST
- SDK and loader
  - Vendor WebView2.h, WebView2EnvironmentOptions.h and the licence from NuGet Microsoft.Web.WebView2 1.0.4191.47. The licence is BSD-3-style (https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Web.WebView2/1.0.4191.47/License); credit it.
  - Ship WebView2Loader.dll next to monolist.exe. WebView2LoaderStatic.lib is MSVC-only (https://github.com/webview/webview README).
  - Load it with LoadLibraryW and GetProcAddress for CreateCoreWebView2EnvironmentWithOptions and GetAvailableCoreWebView2BrowserVersionString.
  - The Qt MinGW kit has wrl/client.h (ComPtr) and eventtoken.h, but no wrl/implements.h or wrl/event.h. So we write one small template that implements IUnknown plus Invoke around std::function for each callback interface, and define the few IIDs we need as constants.
- Threading
  - Everything runs on the GUI thread; Qt has already called OleInitialize there (qwindowscontext.cpp).
  - Nothing blocks. Waits are QTimers, not Metrolist's suspend loop.
- Window
  - A raw Win32 top-level window (CreateWindowExW), owned by the QQuickWindow's HWND, about 480x720 and centred, titled "Sign in - Monolist".
  - WM_SIZE → controller->put_Bounds. WM_CLOSE → flow.cancel().
  - Never overlay it on QML (https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtwebview-index.html).
  - Status, Cancel and "Import cookies instead" live in the existing QML Connections row (views/SettingsView.qml ytmRow, ~L569-692), not inside the web window.
- Profile
  - A fresh throwaway folder for each sign-in: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Monolist\SignIn\<uuid>. It is always local, never on the \\psf share (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/user-data-folder).
  - It never touches the user's Edge profile.
- Settings
  - AreDevToolsEnabled, IsPasswordAutosaveEnabled, IsGeneralAutofillEnabled, AreHostObjectsAllowed, IsWebMessageEnabled, AreDefaultContextMenusEnabled and IsStatusBarEnabled are all false.
  - The user agent is left untouched (honest WebView2 UA), exactly as Metrolist leaves Android's.
- Navigation
  - Navigate to https://accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin?continue=https%3A%2F%2Fmusic.youtube.com.
  - NavigationStarting cancels any non-https scheme. Top-level https navigations outside accounts.google.com, accounts.youtube.com, consent.google.com, consent.youtube.com and *.youtube.com go to the system browser through QDesktopServices; these are help links.
  - NewWindowRequested is handled the same way.
- Success detection
  - NavigationCompleted with IsSuccess on host == music.youtube.com enters Capturing. In the EU a consent.youtube.com page may come first; the user answers it.
  - Every 500 ms, for up to 30 s:
    - ExecuteScript runs a read-only JSON.stringify of ytcfg VISITOR_DATA, DATASYNC_ID, SESSION_INDEX and LOGGED_IN. We never run script on accounts.google.com.
    - ICoreWebView2_2::get_CookieManager → GetCookies("https://music.youtube.com") and GetCookies("https://www.youtube.com") are merged by (name, domain, path). This includes HttpOnly cookies (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/reference/win32/icorewebview2cookiemanager).
    - .google.com cookies are never kept.
  - Accept when (SAPISID or __Secure-3PAPISID) is present and VISITOR_DATA is non-empty. That is Metrolist's rule plus the 3P fallback Monolist already hashes with (src/ytmsession.cpp:577-593).
- Refusal detection
  - If a completed accounts.google.com page matches the "this browser or app may not be secure" rejection, go to Failed(Refused).
  - The exact URL or title is to be learned in the spike; until then, the user can press "Import cookies instead" at any time.
- Tear-down
  - Stop, controller->Close(), release everything, and wait for BrowserProcessExited (ICoreWebView2Environment5).
  - Then delete the profile folder. If that fails, a marker makes the next start sweep it.
  - Closing at once also means no live YouTube tab keeps rotating the captured cookies (yt-dlp wiki advice).
