design.streamingDesign:
PRINCIPLE
- Add one signed-in www.youtube.com rung to the ladder.
- The anonymous rungs stay unchanged and remain the fallback.
- The account never rides on an anonymous request: separate visitor id, separate cookies, and nothing added to the QNetworkAccessManager jar (the rule already in src/innertube.cpp:790-821).

WHY NOT SIMPLY "SIGN IN THE CURRENT TIER"
- Our fast tier is VISIONOS. It cannot carry an account: yt-dlp has visionos SUPPORTS_COOKIES=False (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_base.py), and InnerTubeX marks it unsupported.
- The clients that accept cookies and need no PO token are tv_downgraded (TVHTML5 downgraded) and web_embedded (WEB_EMBEDDED_PLAYER). Both post to https://www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/player, and both return signature-ciphered URLs that need base.js signature and n solving.
- web needs a GVS PO token for https/DASH unless the account is Premium, and it drifts toward SABR (https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12482). Skip it.
- Monolist has no signature/n solver in-process (src/innertube.cpp:979-983). Its yt-dlp tier already runs Deno for exactly that (src/ytdlp.cpp:449-451).

THE RUNG: TierSignedIn (src/streamresolver.h:44-57, a new value right after TierInnerTube)

v1, built on yt-dlp (the first build)
- New YtDlp::resolveAudioSignedIn(videoId, cookieFile), next to resolveAudio (src/ytdlp.cpp:489-500). Arguments:
  - commonArguments (Deno) + URL, --dump-single-json, --no-playlist, -f bestaudio/best;
  - --cookies <file>;
  - --extractor-args youtube:player_client=tv_downgraded,web_embedded (yt-dlp's authed defaults minus web).
- Timeout: the same 12 s guard as the yt-dlp tier.
- yt-dlp itself sends, to www.youtube.com:
  - the .youtube.com cookies;
  - SAPISIDHASH, SAPISID1PHASH and SAPISID3PHASH for origin https://www.youtube.com;
  - X-Goog-AuthUser, X-Origin and the visitor id from the page;
  - the signatureTimestamp, then solves signature and n with Deno.
- The cookie file
  - A new CookieImport::toNetscape(jar) writes only youtube.com-family cookies, never .google.com, to a per-run file in the SecretStore folder under %LOCALAPPDATA% (src/secretstore.h:46).
  - yt-dlp writes the rotated jar back into that file ("dump cookie jar in", https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/README.md). So after each run we parse it with the existing Netscape parser, feed changes to YtmSession::absorbCookies (src/ytmsession.cpp:627), and delete the file.
  - Leftovers are swept at startup.
  - Signed-in runs are serialised, one at a time, so two write-backs never race.
- Media URL
  - mpv gets the googlevideo URL plus yt-dlp's http_headers with any Cookie header removed, as the Muxed tier already takes headers (src/streamresolver.cpp:431).
  - googlevideo.com is not .youtube.com, so no account cookie is needed there. Verify in the spike.
  - The info JSON is never logged, because yt-dlp may carry a cookies field (GHSA-v8mc-9377-rwjj). Only names and counts go to the log.
- Session verdicts
  - The yt-dlp warning "The provided YouTube account cookies are no longer valid" triggers YtmSession::checkNow(). The existing check stays the authority (src/ytmsession.h:26-40).
  - On sessionChanged, drop cached TierSignedIn answers.

v2, native (later, only if v1's roughly 3-4 s per open matters)
- A new InnerTube::Client (TV downgraded) on www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/player, extending the account gate at src/innertube.cpp:794 beyond Client::Music.
- Headers and context:
  - Cookie from header(jar, "www.youtube.com");
  - Authorization with all three SAPISID hashes for origin https://www.youtube.com (already implemented in src/ytmsession.cpp:577-593);
  - X-Origin, Origin and Referer set to https://www.youtube.com;
  - X-Goog-AuthUser = SESSION_INDEX; X-Goog-Visitor-Id = the signed-in VISITOR_DATA;
  - context.user.onBehalfOfUser only for a brand channel;
  - playbackContext.contentPlaybackContext.signatureTimestamp from base.js; contentCheckOk and racyCheckOk set.
- Client constants come from yt-dlp (Unlicense).
- Signature and n are solved by running yt-dlp-ejs (Unlicense, https://api.github.com/repos/yt-dlp/ejs) in the Deno we already ship, with a per-player-version cache. We write this ourselves; InnerTubeX and zemer-cipher are GPL and off-limits.

WHERE IT SITS IN THE LADDER: an owner setting, "Play with my account"
- When needed (recommended default)
  - TierInnerTube (anonymous VISIONOS) runs first.
  - If it fails with LOGIN_REQUIRED (which is how "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" arrives), AGE_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED, AGE_CHECK_REQUIRED or CONTENT_CHECK_REQUIRED (the reasons in src/innertube.cpp:969-977), TierSignedIn goes next.
  - Any other failure tries anonymous TierYtDlp first, then TierSignedIn.
  - After that come Muxed, Piped and Invidious, unchanged.
  - Private and uploaded library items (after C04) go straight to TierSignedIn.
  - The rung is left out of prefetch (src/streamresolver.cpp:256), so tracks that may never play cost no account traffic.
- Always first (what the owner literally asked for)
  - TierSignedIn runs first, then everything else as today, and TierSignedIn joins prefetch to hide its latency.
  - This costs about 3-4 s per open with v1, and it puts every play on the account.
- Off
  - The rung is skipped.
- In every mode, the rung skips itself instantly with "not signed in" when YtmSession is not Active, like empty Piped does (src/streamresolver.cpp:447-450). A signed-out user sees no change.
- A rolling cap, e.g. 120 signed-in resolves per hour, falls through to the anonymous rungs. The owner can tune the number; yt-dlp's wiki cites about 2000/h for accounts and warns of bans.
- Refusals
  - afterRefusal (src/streamresolver.cpp:157-166) gains TierSignedIn → {YtDlp, Muxed, Piped, Invidious}.
  - TierSignedIn is not added to InnerTube's refusal list, because a CDN 403 is about the link, not the account.
- tierLabel shows "YouTube · signed in" (src/playbackcontroller.cpp:45-55).

WHAT IT UNLOCKS
- Age-gated tracks (if the account is age-verified).
- A rescue when YouTube asks the anonymous client to prove it's not a bot.
- Private and uploaded tracks the account can see.
- Higher rate limits.
- Premium: in theory itag 141/774 without a PO token (yt-dlp _DEFAULT_PREMIUM_CLIENTS = web_creator, tv_downgraded, web). Premium formats are currently broken upstream (https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14208, https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17729), so don't chase them yet.
- For a normal account, the audio files are the same as the anonymous ones.

SEQUENCING
- The same enum, startTier, afterRefusal, tierLabel and loadFailed code is being changed on the unmerged jiosaavn branch (checked: jiosaavn is not an ancestor of main 1566fdc).
- Land TierSignedIn after that branch merges, on top of its report() path.

risks: Google may refuse sign-in inside WebView2. Its policy blocks sign-in from browsers embedded in other apps (https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/7675428), and it has blocked embedded frameworks since 2021-01-04 (https://developers.googleblog.com/guidance-to-developers-affected-by-our-effort-to-block-less-secure-browsers-and-applications/). WebView2 reports of 'This browser or app may not be secure' exist (https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/1584, #2552). Enforcement is heuristic: Metrolist's Android WebView works with no UA change, while Tauri/WebView2 apps report mixed results. A search today found no 2026 statement either way. Only the spike can tell, and the answer can change without notice.

Changing the user agent to get past a refusal works against Google's embedded-browser policy. It can also backfire: put_UserAgent may clear the Sec-CH-UA client hints (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/reference/win32/icorewebview2settings2), and Google has been seen rejecting a spoofed Chrome UA whose JavaScript environment does not match (https://github.com/traycerai/traycer/pull/1889). Owner's call, off by default.

Signing in to stream puts the account at risk. yt-dlp's wiki warns that using an account 'you run the risk of it being banned (temporarily or permanently)' (https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors). 'Always first' mode multiplies signed-in requests. Mitigations: 'When needed' is the default, there is an hourly cap, signed-in resolves are left out of prefetch, and the owner should use an account he can afford to lose.

The captured session may not last. YouTube rotates account cookies, and a third-party report puts sessions at days to a few weeks (https://tunelio.dev/blog/yt-dlp-cookies/). Google's Device Bound Session Credentials have been on by default in Chrome on Windows since May 2026 (CONNECTIONS_DESIGN.md:305). Whether the WebView2 runtime registers DBSC, which would bind short-lived cookies to the web view's key so they die once exported, is unverified. Mitigations: close the window immediately, absorb rotated cookies from our own requests and from yt-dlp's write-back, and let the existing check mark the session Expired and ask the user to sign in again.

Secrets end up on disk in two new places: the WebView2 profile folder, and the per-run Netscape cookie file for yt-dlp. Both must live under %LOCALAPPDATA% (never \\psf), be deleted right after use, and be swept at startup. yt-dlp's info JSON may contain a cookies field and must never be logged (https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-v8mc-9377-rwjj).

Toolchain unknowns that have not been checked yet: whether WebView2.h compiles cleanly under the Qt MinGW 13.1 kit (no WRL implements/event headers, __uuidof support), and whether an x64 build runs WebView2 under emulation on this ARM64 VM (runtime 153.0.4234.48 has an x64 folder). WebView2Loader.dll must ship with the app, and its BSD-3 notice must be credited.

The listen ping may not count. Whether a videostatsPlaybackUrl taken from the anonymous VISIONOS response and sent with the account's cookies lands in the account's history is unverified. The fallback costs one extra signed-in WEB_REMIX /player call for each qualified listen.

yt-dlp's signed-in clients (tv_downgraded, web_embedded) are yt-dlp's current defaults but can break at any time, as the upstream issue churn shows. web_embedded fails on videos with embedding disabled. v1 opens take about 3-4 s. Premium 141/774 formats are currently broken upstream (https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14208, #17729).

No server-side sign-out. Removing the account from Monolist does not revoke the Google session (Metrolist does not either). The UI must tell the owner to remove it under Google Account > Security > Your devices.
Refusal detection by URL or title on accounts.google.com is guesswork until the spike records what Google actually shows. That is why the 'Import cookies instead' button stays visible throughout.

Licence contamination. Metrolist, InnerTubeX, zemer-cipher and Lyrenne are GPL-3.0: only behaviour learned from them, no code or structure transcribed. Code-level references must be MIT, BSD or Unlicense: the WebView2 SDK, webview/webview, Kaset, yt-dlp and yt-dlp-ejs.

Merge conflicts with the unmerged jiosaavn branch in streamresolver.*, playbackcontroller.* and main.cpp. The branch has uncommitted edits in C:/dev/monolist-wt/saavn. Land the streaming rung after it merges.

The InnerTubeX details (client flags, which calls carry cookies) came from web fetches of HEAD or v0.7.0, not a local read, so their line numbers are approximate. Nothing in this design depends on them: the Metrolist app code and yt-dlp master were verified directly.

design.spikeFirst:
A half-day standalone probe that proves or disproves the Windows sign-in window before anything goes into Monolist. It lives only in the scratchpad (e.g. ...\scratchpad\signin-probe\), never in the Monolist repo.

Prerequisites (owner)
- OK to download NuGet Microsoft.Web.WebView2 1.0.4191.47 from nuget.org (BSD-3-style licence).
- The owner is at the keyboard to sign in himself, with the account he chooses.

What it is
- About 300 lines of our own C++, built with the Qt MinGW 13.1 kit.
- QGuiApplication supplies the event loop and OleInitialize, exactly as Monolist will.
- A raw Win32 window hosts WebView2. WebView2Loader.dll is loaded with LoadLibraryW.
- Our own IUnknown/Invoke handler template, and hand-defined IIDs if __uuidof fails.
- A throwaway profile under %LOCALAPPDATA%\MonolistProbe\<uuid>.
- DevTools, password autosave and autofill off; the user agent untouched.

Run A: default, honest user agent
1. Navigate to https://accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin?continue=https%3A%2F%2Fmusic.youtube.com. The owner signs in.
2. Log only non-secret facts:
   - each top-level URL's host and path, plus the page title on accounts.google.com, so the refusal page can be recognised if it appears;
   - whether a passkey prompt dead-ends.
3. On NavigationCompleted at music.youtube.com, poll every 500 ms for up to 30 s:
   - ExecuteScript of a read-only ytcfg JSON;
   - GetCookies for https://music.youtube.com and https://www.youtube.com.
4. Print only:
   - cookie NAMES with domain, host-only, HttpOnly and expiry class;
   - whether VISITOR_DATA, DATASYNC_ID and SESSION_INDEX exist, the DATASYNC_ID shape ('X||' or 'X||Y'), and LOGGED_IN.
   Never values.
5. Close the controller, wait for BrowserProcessExited, and delete the profile folder. Confirm the deletion.
6. With the captured jar held in memory, POST https://music.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/account/account_menu as WEB_REMIX with the Cookie and SAPISID hashes. Print only the HTTP status, responseContext logged_in, and whether activeAccountHeaderRenderer is present.
7. Keep the jar DPAPI-encrypted (CryptProtectData) in the probe folder so the same check can re-run at +1 h, +24 h and +72 h. That measures rotation and any DBSC binding. Delete it afterwards.

Run B: only if A is refused and the owner agrees
- The same run with put_UserAgent set to the matching Edge UA. Record whether that is refused too.

Pass criteria
- It compiles with the unmodified SDK headers.
- It runs as an x64 build on this ARM64 VM (runtime 153.0.4234.48).
- Google completes sign-in with the default UA.
- SAPISID or __Secure-3PAPISID and the HttpOnly SID family are captured, along with VISITOR_DATA.
- account_menu reports signed in, and still does at +24 h.

Optional stage B, once A passes, to prove the streaming claim
- Write the jar to a temporary Netscape file.
- Run the already-installed yt-dlp with --cookies and --extractor-args youtube:player_client=tv_downgraded,web_embedded on one age-restricted video the owner picks.
- Print only the playability status, the format count, and whether the googlevideo URL opens with no Cookie header.
- Read the file back to see whether cookies rotated, then delete it.

Outcomes
- A passes: build steps 1-4.
- A fails and B passes: owner decision on the UA.
- Both fail: keep the cookie import as the sign-in and still do the feed and streaming work, which uses the same session.
